result.title: LLMs Depend on Specialist Tools for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in MS/MS Structural Elucidation
authors: Devesh Shah Antonio H. de O. Fonseca
result.comment: Accepted at "NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Agentic Systems for Molecular Sciences" and "I Can't Believe It's Not Better: Failure Modes of AI in Biology Workshop at NeurIPS 2026"
result.summary: A frontier language model was recently reported to solve 1D NMR structural elucidation without tools. We ask whether this capability transfers to tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) in the de novo setting, where the model must propose a structure directly from the spectrum without a candidate list or reference library. To separate reasoning from recall, we build a 100-analyte benchmark from MassSpecGym, split by each analyte's textual footprint into in-distribution (well documented in literature) and out-of-distribution (essentially undocumented) arms. We hold the model, harness, and output format fixed and vary only the LLM's access to domain-specific tools. Without tools, a frontier LLM reaches 52% Top-1 accuracy in-distribution but only 2% out-of-distribution. Only access to de novo structure generators improves out-of-distribution accuracy, raising it to as much as 38% Top-1, and the resulting agent outperforms the standalone de novo models both in and out of distribution. These results suggest that LLMs are not effective at de novo MS/MS structural elucidation on their own, and that further gains depend on the specialist tools available to the agent rather than on the LLM itself.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 MS/MS 去新（de novo）结构解析上构建含 100 个分析物的基准，按文献文本足迹划分为分布内与分布外两臂，固定模型与流程、只改变是否可调用领域工具，衡量前沿 LLM 到底在推理还是在回忆。
AI.relevance_reason: 任务与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「固定模型、仅变外部证据来源」的受控设计与区分记忆和推理的 ID/OOD 划分，可能为核查 VLM 中外部证据获取（如 LOOK）与内部 latent 是否真正承载任务必要信息提供评价范式。
